paragraphs: Friend, Proverbs 27 is a box of short sayings, and when I step back, I see one thread running through all of them: stay humble and stay close. Solomon says, "Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring." (Proverbs 27:1) He also says, "Let another praise you, and not your own mouth" (Proverbs 27:2), and that a man is tested by the praise accorded him (Proverbs 27:21). So the lesson is simple: we don't hold tomorrow, and a little praise can go to our heads faster than hot dough goes to a cooling rack.

The second thing this chapter teaches is that good people make us better, even when it stings. "Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed." (Proverbs 27:5) "The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful." (Proverbs 27:6) And "As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another." (Proverbs 27:17) I think that means a real friend is worth keeping close, the kind who shows up when your day of calamity comes, because Solomon says "better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away." (Proverbs 27:10)

The last thing is to pay attention to what is in front of you. The prudent see danger and take cover, and the simple keep going and pay the penalty (Proverbs 27:12). Solomon tells us to know the state of our flocks, because "riches are not forever" (Proverbs 27:23-24). So, friend, today is a good day to ask who is sharpening you, who you are sharpening, and what you have been given to look after. Don't wait on tomorrow for that, because you do not know what a day may bring.
